City Council  CONSIDERATION OF STATEMENT ON FEDERAL ACTIVITY
  AND COMMUNITY REASSURANCE IN PASADENA (Office of the
  Mayor)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is covered
  by the "Common Sense" exemption set forth in the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3)
  as CEQA only applies to projects that may have a significant effect
  on the environment;
  (2) Approve the Statement on Federal Activity and Community
  Reassurance in Pasadena.

Council Minutes  6  06/23/2025
   City Attorney Bagneris reported that the City Council may approve
  the proposed statement at an open and public City Council meeting,
  which may cure any potential issues related to the Brown Act.

  Pablo Alvarado, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns
  regarding the recent federal immigration raids and urged the City
  Council to take the following actions in response to federal
  operations: 1) adopt an ordinance protecting civil rights and
  human rights for all Pasadenans, 2) create an immigrant
  defense fund, 3) use law enforcement and public safety
  resources to protect those in danger when unidentifiable agents
  swarm the streets, 4) stop unnecessary policing practices that
  may cause tensions and fear in the community, 5) adopt a zero
  tolerance policy for federal agents and dangerous activities if
  ICE vehicles and drivers endanger lives or public order, 6)
  explain any and all agreements the City may have with ICE or
  other enforcement agencies, 7) conduct a full and transparent
  investigation of the masked gunman who drew his weapon on a
  civilian during an immigration raid on Orange Grove Blvd, and 8)
  address how the City will work to protect its immigrant
  community in light of hosting the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup.

  The following individuals expressed concerns regarding the recent
  federal immigration enforcement activities in the City and urged the
  City Council to take actions to protect the City's immigrant
  community and/or provided other related comments:

Council Minutes  7  06/23/2025
   Councilmember Madison expressed support for the adopting the
  proposed statement and advocated for the City to take action.

  Vice Mayor Rivas also expressed support for the proposed
  statement and for the City taking action, and emphasized the
  importance of moral clarity, standing in solidarity with immigrant
  communities, and recognizing that the federal administration's
  actions threaten democracy.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry, Brenda Harvey-
  Williams, Assistant City Manager, confirmed that the City does offer
  services that provide residents with information on how to obtain
  citizenship and filling out various government forms at Jackie
  Robinson Community Center and Villa Park Community Center. He
  advocated for the City to reach out to congressional representatives
  to address the matter and send letters urging for humanity,
  highlighting the economic impacts and advocating for due process.

  Mayor Gordo advocated for the City and the nonprofit community to
  create a fund that would support and assist families that are
  impacted by immigration raids.

  Councilmember Lyon reiterated that the City's law enforcement does
  not participate in, nor cooperate with, any immigration enforcement,
  and emphasized that the City is working to identify lawful ways to
  address the matter while preserving the rule of law. He also
  expressed support for the newly proposed State Senate Bill 805 -
  No Vigilantes Act, aimed at holding law enforcement accountable
  and increasing transparency during immigration enforcement
  actions.

  Councilmember Cole advocated for local organizations and bodies
  (i.e. Tournament of Roses, Chamber of Commerce, One Pasadena,
  Pasadena City College, etc.) to work together and help the
  community during these unprecedented times.

  Mayor Gordo reflected on his family's journey of immigrating to the
  United States and settling in Pasadena. He emphasized the
  importance of the contributions from immigrants in all aspects and
  the harms of stigmatizing an entire community. He noted that the
  City's Police Department is in communication with federal agencies
  to determine if federal operations are in fact legitimate. He thanked
  the community for speaking out in a respectful, safe, and peaceful
  manner.

  MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Hampton,
  seconded by Councilmember Jones, to approve the proposed
  statement, with direction to the Finance Committee to discuss
  creating an immigrant assistance fund in collaboration with the
  nonprofit community organizations, and refer to the Legislative

RECOMMENDATIONS  APPOINTMENT OF THREE COMMUNITY-BASED
FROM OFFICERS AND  ORGANIZATION NOMINEES TO THE COMMUNITY POLICE
DEPARTMENTS  OVERSIGHT COMMISSION (City Attorney/City Prosecutor's Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
City Attorney  (1) Find that the proposed action in the agenda report is not a
  project subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to Section 21065 of CEQA and Sections
  15060(c)(2),15060(c)(3), and 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines,
  and as such, no environmental document pursuant to CEQA is
  required; and
  (2) Review the six applications received for the Community Police
  Oversight Commission (CPOC) community-based organization
  seats and appoint three community-based organization nominees to
  the CPOC for 3-year terms beginning on July 1, 2025, as further
  described in the Agenda Report.

  Mayor Gordo provided a brief overview on the CROC'S scope of work
  and their purpose to strengthen community police relations.

  Shannon Prior, Principal Administrative Analyst, provided a brief
  overview of the three community-based organization vacancies on
  the CPOC, the recruitment process, and the appointment process.

Council Minutes  9  06/23/2025
   In response to Councilmember Madison's inquiry regarding potential
  conflicts of interests to serve on the Commission, City Attorney
  Bagneris reported that a nominee's law enforcement background is
  not codified as a disqualifying factor in the Pasadena Municipal Code
  from serving on the Community Police Oversight Commission. She
  also clarified that letters of recommendations for applicants are not
  a requirement when applying.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that one letter expressing support for
  Andrea McCraw, one letter expressing support for Faisal Rashid,
  twenty-two letters expressing support for Latoya Patillo, and one
  letter expressing support for Ted Smith, were all received by the City
  Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council, posted online, and
  made part of the public record.

  Alexandra Annala, Latoya Patillo, Andrea McCraw, Faisal Rashid,
  Ted Smith, and Olden Denham individually participated in an
  interview process, providing an overview of each applicant's
  experience and qualification, and responded to questions posed by
  the City Council.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, advocated for the CPOC to hold
  police officers accountable and receive public input to improve
  public safety.

  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City Council
  to select an applicant who will work to improve community
  police relations, noting his support for Olden Denham.

  The following individuals spoke in support of Latoya Patillo to be
  appointed to the CPOC:

  Sydney Pierce, residence not stated
  Mark Sutton, Pasadena residence
  Paula Norwood, Pasadena resident
  June Carr, Monrovia resident

  Esprit Jones, Pasadena resident, shared that the CPOC has
  worked to improve community relations with the Pasadena
  Police Department, and urged community members to show up
  and express their concerns when necessary, so that the
  Community Police Oversight Commission can address them.

  Brandon Lamar, Pasadena resident, spoke on the purpose of
  the CPOC and the importance of building bridges between law
  enforcement and the community.

  Heavenly Hughes, My Tribe Rise, expressed concerns with the
  lack of community awareness regarding the new appointments
  being made to the CPOC.

Council Minutes  10  06/23/2025
   The City Council deliberated and reported their top selections to the
  three community-based organizational appointments to the CPOC.

  MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Lyon,
  seconded by Councilmember Cole, to appoint Latoya Patillo, Ted
  Smith, and Faisal Rashid, to the three community-based
  organizational seats to the CPOC.

  Vice Mayor Rivas urged Mr. Faisal Rashid to focus on residents'
  experiences and perspectives, and less so from personal experience
  in law enforcement, when serving as a commissioner on the CPOC.

  AYES: Councilmembers Cole, Hampton, Jones, Lyon,
  Madison, Masuda, Vice Mayor Rivas, Mayor Gordo
